test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: How are the whales protected naturally?

options.text: By having the habitat of the Arctic sea
By the presence of a thick fat covering

solution:
The correct answer is **"By the presence of a thick fat covering". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage specifies that to protect whales from the cold Arctic seas, nature has equipped them with blubber, a thick layer of fat.
 
• Blubber acts as an insulator, helping whales maintain their body temperature in the cold waters.
 
• This covering is not only important for thermal insulation but also serves as an energy reserve for the whale.
 
• The passage does not mention the oil-producing quality, size, or habitat as natural protections, specifically emphasizing the role of the thick fat covering.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **By their oil producing quality** - This option is incorrect because the passage indicates that the oil is a product derived from whales, not a mechanism of protection.
 
• **By their huge size - **While the size of whales may deter some predators, the passage explicitly attributes their protection in cold Arctic seas to their blubber, not their size.
 
• **By having the habitat of the Arctic sea **- Living in the Arctic sea is a fact about the whales' environment but is not stated as a means of natural protection. It's the blubber that protects them in this habitat.
